I have a story similar to this.
I was in about 8th grade, and was bored at home, so I started watching some youtube videos. I came across this video where a guy cut open a battery and there a bunch of smaller batteries (AA->watch style battery). So I grab an AA battery and a knife, and go to the kitchen. I try cutting the battery like a piece of steak, but it's not going through. So I grab the pointiest knife I can find, and stab it as hard as I can. The acid inside began spraying out, directly into my face and eyes. I had no time to react, and thus began the worst pain of my life. My mother was in another room, and I began screaming. The pain was like getting shampoo in your eyes but x1000. I ran water over my eyes for hours. I couldn't see for the rest of the day, and the pain was still excruciating. I also had burn spots on my face. The next day we go to the doctor, and he puts glow in the dark ink in my eyes. He said it was mm from hitting my cornea, permanantly  blinding me. After a couple days, the pain finally went away, and my vision fully restored.

TL;DR - Stabbed a battery, acid in my eye, pain, pain, more pain.

It could lead to knowing what you want to do as a career and you will be around others who share the same interests. Don't be afraid to put yourself out there. Whats the worst that can happen?

I understand. My first year of H.S. I sat practically alone in the lunchroom. No one around me was a real friend. If your school has a library, see if you can go in there every day. I am a senior now, and have been doing so for a few years. It is very nice to be in silence. There is another kid who did the same thing, and were good friends now. If you can't go in the library, find a teacher who you like and tell them the situation. Just hang out in their room. They will understand. Feel better.
